legend: One day, Alice challenged Bob with the interactive programming problem described below.

You have a tree (an acyclic connected graph). Each node of the tree has exactly one parent, except the root node, which has no parent. Nodes that are not parents of any nodes are called leaves. You know the structure of the tree, because you know the parent of each node that is not the root.

Each node contains an integer value. A node that is not a leaf contains the sum of the values of all its direct children. Thus, all the values in the tree are determined by the values contained in the leaves.
The picture below depicts an example. The leaves are marked as gray, while the other nodes are white. Each node shows the value it contains.
Initially, you don't know any of the node values, but you can query them one by one. Your task is to figure out the value of each node in the tree, making as few queries as possible.

Bob solved this problem very easily. Then, to spice things up, Alice asked him: "given the tree structure, how many different solutions to this problem exist?" That is, how many different minimal sets of queries exist that allow one to figure out all the values stored in the tree? (Two sets of queries are considered different if and only if there is a node that is queried in one set but not in the other.)
input: The tree has N$$$N$$$ nodes in total. Each node is identified by an integer between 1$$$1$$$ and N$$$N$$$, where node 1$$$1$$$ is the root.
The input consists of two lines. The first line contains only the integer N$$$N$$$.

The second line contains N−1$$$N-1$$$ integers P1,P2,…,PN−1$$$P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{N-1}$$$, separated by a single space, where Pi$$$P_i$$$ is the parent of node i+1$$$i + 1$$$, for i=1,2,…,N−1$$$i = 1, 2, \ldots, N - 1$$$.
output: The output consists of a single line, which must contain the number of different minimal solutions to the problem faced by Bob. As this number may be large, your answer must be calculated mod 1000000007$$$1000000007$$$ (109+7)$$$(10^9 + 7)$$$.

legend.ai: 一天，Alice 向 Bob 提出了下面所描述的交互式编程问题。
你有一棵树（一个无环连通图）。树中的每个节点恰好有一个父节点，根节点除外，根节点没有父节点。不作为任何节点父节点的节点称为叶子。由于你知道每个非根节点的父节点，因此你知道这棵树的结构。
每个节点中都包含一个整数值。非叶节点中的值等于其所有直接子节点的值之和。因此，树中的所有值都由叶节点中的值决定。
下图展示了一个例子。叶子节点标记为灰色，而其他节点为白色。每个节点都显示其包含的值。
起初，你不知道任何节点的值，但可以逐个查询它们。你的任务是用尽可能少的查询，确定树中每个节点的值。
Bob 很容易地解决了这个问题。然后，为了增添趣味，Alice 问他：“给定树的结构，解决这个问题的不同方案有多少种？”也就是说，有多少个不同的最小查询集合，可以据此确定树中存储的所有值？（当且仅当存在某个节点在一个集合中被查询而在另一个集合中未被查询时，才认为两个查询集合不同。）

input.ai: 这棵树总共有 N$$$N$$$ 个节点。每个节点都由一个介于 1$$$1$$$ 和 N$$$N$$$ 之间的整数标识，其中节点 1$$$1$$$ 是根节点。
输入由两行组成。第一行只包含整数 N$$$N$$$。
第二行包含 N−1$$$N-1$$$ 个整数 P1,P2,…,PN−1$$$P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_{N-1}$$$，它们由单个空格分隔，其中，Pi$$$P_i$$$ 是节点 i+1$$$i + 1$$$ 的父节点(i=1,2,…,N−1$$$i = 1, 2, \ldots, N - 1$$$)。

output.ai: 输出由一行组成，其中必须包含 Bob 所面对问题的不同最小解的数量。由于该数可能很大，你的答案必须对 1000000007$$$1000000007$$$ (109+7)$$$(10^9 + 7)$$$ 取模。
